why: A free function's declared `this` parameter is its receiver: its self type is the declared type, a first operand. sum reorders the sum: proved. shifted reads another field: witnessed. viaHelper calls a method of the receiver on both sides (an outside call on the operand): proved. climb keeps the unbounded loop (one transition taking the receiver) and doubles by an addition: proved. climbOther bounds the loop by another field: a different transition, witnessed. pages pages through the receiver's fetch on both sides: proved. bump writes the receiver inside the loop (the receiver is an output of the block) and reads it after through a local: proved. bumpRead reads the field before the loop: not proved, witnessed. bumpVia binds the receiver with call and inherits bumpRead's change: witnessed. tally keeps a counted loop that reads the receiver (the loop helper takes it as a const operand) and doubles by an addition: proved. tallyOther reads another field in the loop: witnessed.
